chunks: Humayd, from Ibn Sama'ah, from Ja'far ibn Sama'ah, from Dawud ibn Sirhan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) — similar to it.

Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, who said: I asked him (peace be upon him) about the divorced woman, where she waits. He (peace be upon him) said: In her house, she should not go out; and if she wants to visit, she goes out after midnight, and does not go out during the day, and it is not for her to perform Hajj until her waiting period has expired.
And I asked him (peace be upon him) about the one whose husband died, is she like that? He (peace be upon him) said: Yes, and she performs Hajj if she wishes.
ai.seo_question: What are the differences in waiting period rules between a divorced woman and a widow regarding staying home and performing Hajj?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), transmitted via the reliable chain of Samaan ibn Mehran, clarifies the distinction between the seclusion of a divorced woman and the relative freedom of a widow during their respective waiting periods. It highlights the practical application of *iddah* by permitting night-time exits for visits while restricting daytime movement for the divorced, whereas the widow retains the right to perform Hajj immediately, reflecting the different social and economic statuses implied in Shia jurisprudence.

en.hubeali: Humeyd, from Ibn Sama’at, from Ja’far Bin Sama’at, from Dawood Bin Sirhan, from Abu Abdullahasws – similar to it.

Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Usman Bin Isa, from sama’at Bin Mihran who said, 
‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the divorced woman, from where she waits. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘In her house, she should not go out; and if she wants to visit, she should go out from after midnight, and not to go out by day, and it is not for her that she should go for Hajj until she has fulfilled her waiting period’.
And I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the one widowed from her husband, is she like that?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, but she can go to Hajj if she so desires to’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Sama‘ah ibn Mehran who has said the following:

“I once asked him (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a woman who is divorced and about where she must complete her waiting period. He (the Imam) said, ‘She completes her waiting period in her house and must not go out. If she wants to visit she must go after midnight but not during the day. She does not have the right to perform al-Hajj until her waiting period is complete.’
I asked about one whose husband dies; if her case is the same. He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, it is the same but she can perform al-Hajj if she wants.’”
